1 October 2025 NEWS FROM THE BOARD June 2026 NEWS FROM THE BOARD A monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. Ryan Davidson - Commissioner Tom Dayley - Commissioner Rod Beck - Chairman

2 ADA COUNTY EMPLOYEES SHOW UP TO CELEBRATE AMERICA 250 Group photo to be buried in a time capsule later this year Ada County employees gathered on a warm evening on June 18th for a group photo that will be buried later this year in a 50-year time capsule. This is all part of the county’s ongoing efforts to recognize and celebrate the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. The photo was taken at the Ridges Bridge at Ada County’s Park at Expo Idaho scheduled to open October 23, 2026. Thank you to all the county employees, and elected officials who participated in this gesture of respect and celebration. Stay tuned for details of when the Ada County time capsule will be buried. Hint: It’s on Ada County’s 162nd birthday.

4 FLOAT SEASON 2026 OPENS WITH BLUE SKIES AND WARM TEMPERATURES Float Season Kickoff News Conference The wait is over! Float the Boise is back for 2026. The Ada County Commissioners - Chairman Rod Beck and Commissioner Tom Dayley, along with Ada County Sheriff Matt Clifford, Ada County Parks & Waterways, Boise Parks and Recreation and Boise Fire Department were happy to announce the kickoff of the 2026 Boise River float season late last month. Thank you to Ada County Parks & Waterways Director Scott Koberg and his staff for always making the kickoff news conference enjoyable and informative.

# Page 5^page=5
5 Ready to float? Visit floattheboise.org for river conditions, shuttle information, rentals, maps, and safety resources. Before you hit the water: • Wear a life jacket (required for children 14 and under) • Never tie rafts or tubes together • Bring a paddle to help navigate obstacles • Pack out what you pack in

6 CHAIRMAN ROD BECK SPEAKS AT BOISE METRO ROTARY Presentation centered on Ada County’s Park at Expo Idaho Coming in Late October If you haven’t heard about Ada County’s Park at Expo Idaho, which opens in late October, you may be in the middle of a news cleanse. This 49+ acre park was the focus of a presentation given by Chairman Rod Beck to the Boise Metro Rotary on June 23rd – exactly four months from the opening date October 23, 2026. Speaking to civic groups gives the Ada County Commissioners the opportunity to share details of what’s happening in Idaho’s largest county by population. Thank you for being an inquisitive audience, with great questions. If your organization, neighborhood group or club would like to hear from the Ada County Commissioners please email eduncan@adacounty.id.gov

■ EMERGENCY JUNE 2026 PREPAREDNESS POINTER ]PET PREPAREDNESS[ Many public shelters and hotels will not allow pets inside their facilities, even during times of emergency, due to concerns of public health, hygiene, safety, and lack of accommodations. Because of this, it is important to plan � what you are going to do with your pets before an emergency occurs. PLAN FOR YOUR PET PET EMERGENCY KIT ¢ °¢ doe A The following should be considered when planning for your pets: Plan with relatives, friends, and trusted neighbors who would be willing to allow your family and pets to shelter at their residence during an emergency or who would at least be willing to take care of your pets while you cannot. Contact local animal shelters, veterinary clinics, and boarding kennels to see if they take pets during emergencies or if they know of locations that do. Contact hotels outside your immediate area to see if they would allow pets during an emergency. Much like an emergency kit you would assemble for yourself, make sure to assemble one for your pet as well with necessities that will last at least 72-96 hours. Items to consider putting in a pet emergency kit may include: � Food � Water � Collar with ID tag / Leash � Traveling bag, crate, or carrier , � Grooming items � Food/Water bowls (shampoo, brush, � Can opener � Medicine � First aid kit � nail clippers etc.) � Sanitation needs (pet litter, newspapers, trash bags, etc.) � Familiar items (toys, treats, bedding, etc.) � Recent picture of you and your pet together � Vaccination records DON'T FORGET! Keep your pet's microchip information up to date, including your phone number and an emergency contact outside of your immediate area. � A LITTLE PLANNING TODAY CAN KEEP YOUR PET SAFE TOMORROW. 8 IMPORTANT SURVEY - TAKES 5 MINUTES ADA COUNTY GOVERNMENT In addition to elected offices, Ada County government includes twelve individual departments. Each department provides important services to our residents in Star, Eagle, Meridian, Boise, Garden City, Kuna, and Unincorporated Ada County. These services include law enforcement protection, emergency preparedness, election services, parks & waterways, indigent services, juvenile services, solid waste management, the Western Idaho Fair, Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement and more. Learn more about the services provided to you by Ada County - www.adacounty.id.gov/

# Page 9^page=9
9 TRACY ROBERTS - 20 YEARS OF EXCEPTIONAL SERVICE Tracy Roberts has been an exceptional asset to the Records Retention Center for the past 20 years, including the last 10 years serving as supervisor. Throughout her tenure, Tracy has consistently demonstrated professionalism, accuracy, reliability, and a remarkable level of dedication to both her team and the departments she supports. The work performed within records retention requires tremendous attention to detail, consistency, and accountability. Under Tracy’s leadership, the operation has functioned with an extraordinarily high level of accuracy and efficiency. The courts and numerous county departments rely heavily on her team’s ability to retrieve, process, digitize, and maintain records in a timely and dependable manner, and Tracy has ensured that standard is not only met, but exceeded. Tracy has built and maintained a team culture centered around accountability, cooperation, and service. She leads with quiet competence and consistency, creating an environment where work is completed thoroughly, correctly, and without unnecessary oversight or issues. In an area where precision matters immensely, her operation has proven to be nearly flawless. Beyond her work ethic and leadership, Tracy brings personality and warmth to the workplace in a way that genuinely impacts the people around her. Her infectious laugh can carry across the office and instantly lighten the mood, even during the busiest days. She has a way of making people feel comfortable, supported, and welcome, which speaks volumes about the kind of person she is. And of course, no description of Tracy would be complete without mentioning her well-known love of Rob Lowe — a running source of humor and conversation that has become part of her trademark charm around the office. In addition to her technical knowledge and operational leadership, Tracy is simply an outstanding person to work with. She is dependable, approachable, professional, and deeply respected by those who interact with her. Over the years, she has earned the trust and appreciation of countless employees across the county through her responsiveness, positive attitude, and unwavering commitment to doing things the right way. Tracy’s long-standing commitment to the county, the court system, and the integrity of records management deserves significant recognition. She represents the type of employee every organization hopes to have: experienced, trustworthy, team- oriented, and consistently excellent at what she does. Twenty years in records retention without drama, chaos, or mistakes piling up is basically the government-operations equivalent of pitching a perfect game while alphabetizing the archives at the same time.

10 CONGRATULATIONS ROD MURPHY ON YOUR 25 YEARS OF SERVICE TO ADA COUNTY For 25 years, Rod Murphy has served as an exceptional role model and inspired hope as a Juvenile Detention Officer. During a quarter-century of dedicated service, Rod has demonstrated an unwavering commitment to guiding youth through their most challenging moments. Rod takes the time to provide individual mentoring and leads group sessions that teach crucial life lessons juveniles can carry with them long after they leave. Beyond his impact on the youth, Rod is a phenomenal coworker who brings a positive attitude to the facility and is always willing to step up and help others. Pictured L-R: Heather Chapman, Ada County Juvenile Services Division Manager, Richard Maher, Ada County Juvenile Services Assistant Division Manager for Juvenile Detention, Ada County Commissioner Tom Dayley, Rod Murphy, Juvenile Detention Officer, Miranda Murphy (Rod’s Daughter), Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck, and Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson
